So, defying all odds, Bangladesh have batted nearly one-and-a-half days to keep New Zealand at bay and also put on a good total. The question is, will they declare overnight? Or will they continue to bat for as long as they can? The first session tomorrow is an extended one as well, so they might take that into consideration. Do join us at 0300 IST (2130 GMT, previous day) for the action from Day 3. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed, there will be NO COMMENTARY for this game. But we will provide you with updates at the end of the day. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!
The home side had to struggle for wickets. Boult and Southee got 2 wickets apiece while Wagner got three towards the end. The Kiwis would have got more wickets, but for the dropped catches.

The good thing about the stand was that it took very few balls, only 494 balls to be precise. The counter-attack from Shakib took them off completely and he went on to score a mammoth 217. Rahim himself made a fine 159 to take the score past 500.

There were only two overs left for the day and hence, with that wicket, it is STUMPS ON DAY 2! What a day for the visitors. They started it poorly, losing Mominul very early, but then a massive 359-run stand for the 5th wicket between Shakib and Rahim put the Kiwis on the back foot.

Tomorrow play will start half an hour early, at 0230 IST (2100 GMT, previous day). Hopefully, we will have more cricketing action. Join us then. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed, we WILL NOT BE ABLE to provide you with commentary. But there will be a few updates. Adios! Take Care!

The Kiwis tried hard but rain did not allow them to settle. Trent Boult struck early but then the home side struggled to break through. Constant rain breaks did not help them either. They could have had Shakib before stumps but then Santner dropped a sitter. They will look to come back hard tomorrow and try and bowl out the Bangladeshis quickly.
Tamim got a useful half century while Mahmudullah put in an 85-run stand with Mominul. The "Bangladeshi Bradman" has looked composed for his 64 and not flustered at all.

Not a bad day at all for Bangladesh. After being asked to bat on a green and lively pitch, one would have expected the visitors to fade out quickly and an early loss of Imrul Kayes only strengthened that case. But Tamim Iqbal, Mominul Haque and later Mahmudullah fought hard to keep the Kiwis at bay.

Team news - TASKIN AHMED and SUBASHIS ROY will debut for Bangladesh while TIM SOUTHEE and TRENT BOULT are back in the side for the hosts.
TOSS - Kane Williamson flips the coin, Mushfiqur Rahim calls it wrong. And as expected, NEW ZEALAND WILL BOWL!

Bangladesh are yet to register a win on this tour and will have a herculean task ahead of them as they head into this one. Mustafizur Rahman is out rested for the opening Test and Taskin Ahmed in all likelihood will be leading the bowling attack in his debut match. The weather is expected to remain overcast with showers predicted later in the day but let's hope nothing as such happens. If such are the conditions the captains would want to win the toss and have a go with the ball. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed there won't be any commentary for this game but we will provide you with each day's update after stumps.

Hello and a warm welcome for the first game of the two-match Test series between New Zealand and Bangladesh. The hosts will be riding high on confidence after outclassing the Asian minnows in the coloured clothing and come this series they would only look to stamp their authority further. Southee and Boult are back and for sure they will be the force to be reckoned with given the conditions. Also, Ross Taylor, the veteran will be back in the side which will only boost the morale of the Kiwis.
